---
title: "Overview"
guide-section: "Start Here"
---

tether is version control for datasets that live in several systems at once:
an Icechunk repository here, a directory of raw files there, a Postgres
database, an Iceberg table, the code that produced them. It keeps one small
manifest per object in a git or jj repository. A commit of those manifests is
a complete, reproducible position for every object -- and, where the system
allows it, tether *pins* that position with a native ref so it stays readable,
and *forks* a writable branch off it when you want to change things safely.

## The loop

```bash
tether init                          # inside a git or jj repository
tether add zarr/imaging --kind icechunk s3://bucket/imaging.icechunk
tether add raw/plate1   --kind file     s3://bucket/raw/plate1/
tether commit -m "Baseline"          # record every object; pin what can be pinned

tether new -b relabel                # a branch in every system, forked on first write
python relabel.py                    # write through repo.open("zarr/imaging")
tether commit -m "Relabel plate1"    # pin the branch heads; move the bookmark
tether promote                       # land it on main, in every system at once
```

Reading back is one flag: `tether open zarr/imaging --rev <commit>` (or
`TETHER_REV=<commit>` for a whole job) hands you the system's native handle at
exactly the state that commit recorded.

## Vocabulary

Eight words carry the whole guide.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **object** | One thing tether tracks, under a key such as `zarr/imaging`: an Icechunk repository, a directory or object-store prefix, a Neon database, a git repository, ... |
| **dataset** | The git/jj repository holding one manifest per object. A **dataset commit** is a VCS commit of those manifests: a position for every object at once. |
| **state** | An object's fingerprint right now -- a snapshot id, an LSN, a content digest. Comparing states is how drift is found. |
| **pin** | A durable native ref (`tether.<dataset>.<hash>`: an Icechunk tag, a Neon branch, a git tag) that tether creates at commit time so a recorded state cannot be expired or garbage-collected. |
| **bookmark** | A jj bookmark or git branch of the dataset. It stands for one branch per system. |
| **trunk** | The `main` bookmark. It stands for each object's **upstream branch** -- the branch the object had before tether -- so working on the trunk writes there. |
| **working ref** | The store branch this checkout writes through: the upstream branch on the trunk, `tether.ws.<dataset>.<bookmark>` on any other bookmark. |
| **fork** | A writable branch created off a pin, the first time a bookmark writes to an object. |

Backends fall into four **tiers** by what they can do with a state: *Observed*
(fingerprint only), *Addressable* (re-read later by id), *Pinnable* (a native
ref holds it), *Forkable* (a branch can be made from it). The
[Backends](09-backends.qmd) page lists every system's tier.
